packet.title: near-approval spec review
packet.summary: What a spec reviewer reads and signs to discharge ASM-SPEC for the NEAR approval contract. The reviewer certifies that the specs say what the contract is meant to do: the property statements and the reference step semantics. The proofs re-run in CI on every change; the reviewer reads statements and skips proof bodies.
packet.qualifies: A named human who did not write approval-core. Claude sessions wrote most of the specs and harnesses, so a review by Claude does not count.
why_a_day: The step semantics is written four times (Prolog step/4, TLA+, Lean, the Verus spec machine) and machines check that the copies agree: MC-3 and MC-4 (Prolog graph = TLC graph = Lean graph, 21,670 stores, 41,706 edges); MC-2, RT-TRACE and REF-5 (210 traces, 6,800 steps, identical on the real core, spec.rs, tla.rs and the deployed wasm); Verus (the core refines abs.rs for every public function).

So the reviewer reads one copy of the step semantics closely (item C) and spot-checks the rest. Property statements are tied together only by shared IDs, C-7 traceability and mutants, so those are what need reading.

items.title: Contract intent (README)
items.summary: The contract README is the statement of intent. Everything in the later items must agree with it.
check: You understand what each of the 16 #[near] methods is for, who may call it, and what it records.
Nothing in the README is ambiguous enough that two readers would build different contracts.

items.title: Threats and property catalogue
items.summary: strategy.md section 3 (threats, trust assumptions) and section 5 (the property catalogue in math). Each property must mean what the README means.
check: Each property in section 5 states what the README means; none over-claims or under-claims.
Nothing the README promises is missing from section 5.
Section 3.2 maps every listed threat to at least one property.

items.title: Reference step semantics (Prolog step/4)
items.summary: The requirements-only Prolog machine. The TLC and Lean state graphs are machine-checked equal to it, and its traces are replayed on the real core and the wasm, so this is the one copy of the step semantics to read closely.
check: The guard order and the error each guard raises match the README for add_agent/add_approver, revoke_key, request_action, approve and reject.
The effects of each successful step (what is written, what counters move) match the README.

items.title: Verus spec machine and lemma statements
items.summary: The strongest evidence: a proof on the real core at every store size. Read abs.rs in full and only the ensures clauses (statements) of the lemma files.
check: The spec machine in abs.rs matches step/4 (item C).
Each lemma statement matches its section 5 row.

items.title: What Verus takes on trust
items.summary: Every assume_specification, external type spec and trusted impl the verified twin relies on, and every rewrite of deployed code inside the twin.

read.label: Trusted specs, each mapped to an ASM

check: Each trusted std/near-sdk spec holds for the pinned toolchain and near-sdk 5.29.1.
Each rewrite is behaviour-preserving (each has a Kani equivalence harness).

items.title: TLA+ property statements
items.summary: The TLA+ invariants, action properties and liveness formulas.
check: INV, HIST and liveness formulas match their section 5 rows.

items.title: Lean property statements and temporal encoding
items.summary: Lean proves the TLA+ model's properties at every size. Read the statements and the one-line encodings of the TLA+ temporal operators.

read.label: Temporal encoding (Steps, EvAlways, InfOften, Enabled, WeakFair, StrongFair) and Live1

check: The Lean statements say what the TLA+ ones say.
Steps, EvAlways, InfOften, Enabled, WeakFair and StrongFair match TLA+ semantics.

items.title: Kani executable spec (spec.rs)
items.summary: Kani checks the deployed code path within bounds, and L2 lifts that to every store size. Mostly redundant with D1; skim it.
check: expected agrees with step/4 (spot-check 3 operations).

items.title: Trust assumptions
items.summary: Every assumption the verification rests on, against strategy.md section 3.3. ASM-FINAL, ASM-TOOLS, ASM-OWNER and ASM-DISPLAY are trusted permanently by decision.
check: Each assumption is acceptable for this deployment.
The permanently trusted list (ASM-FINAL, ASM-TOOLS, ASM-OWNER, ASM-DISPLAY) is agreed.

items.title: near-sdk macro expansion (SH-9, RD-6)
items.summary: The #[near] wrapper is generated code that unit tests cannot see. Run cargo expand on the contract at the pin and read the wrapper.
check: #[init] new panics if state already exists, and is #[private].
Every method fails before init (PanicOnDefault).
Change methods are non-payable.
&self view methods never write state.
Only the 16 #[near] methods are exported.

items.title: Open findings accepted as documented
items.summary: Findings that stay open by design. Each is either defence in depth or covered by a property or deployment rule.
check: Each finding below is acceptable with the resolution path given.
